headline: Margins compress, earnings fall, but deliveries hit target
summary_short: Lennar reported Q2 FY2026 revenue of $7.94 billion (-5.2% y/y) and diluted EPS of $1.24, down from $1.81, as gross margin on home sales fell to 15.6% from 17.8% amid soft pricing and elevated incentives.
summary_long: Revenue fell 5.2% y/y to $7.94B as Multifamily and Financial Services revenue declined alongside a 5% drop in average home sales price to $371,000, partly offset by 2% more deliveries (20,519 homes). Homebuilding gross margin fell to 15.6% from 17.8% on lower revenue per square foot and higher land costs, partly offset by lower construction costs; SG&A rose to 9.2% of home-sale revenue on deleverage. Financial Services operating earnings fell to $101M on lower mortgage profit per loan. Net earnings fell 36% to $305M ($1.24/share, $1.31 excluding tech-investment mark-to-market losses). Lennar held $1.8B cash, no revolver borrowings, and repurchased $447M of stock. Q3 2026 guidance: 20,500-21,500 deliveries, ~16% gross margin; full-year delivery target trimmed to ~82,000-83,000 homes.

drivers.explanation: Total revenue fell as Multifamily and Financial Services revenue declined and average home sales price fell 5%, partly offset by a 2% increase in home deliveries.
Homebuilding gross margin on home sales fell to 15.6% from 17.8% on lower revenue per square foot and higher land costs, partly offset by a decrease in construction costs.

Homebuilding SG&A rose to 9.2% of home-sale revenue from 8.8% on lower revenue leverage and higher marketing spend; Financial Services operating earnings also fell on lower mortgage profit per locked loan.
Decline mirrors lower Homebuilding and Financial Services operating earnings, plus $23M of mark-to-market losses on technology investments within Lennar Other.
EPS fell less than net income in percentage terms because diluted weighted-average shares fell about 7.5% y/y (260.3M to 240.8M) from continued buybacks.
Declined in line with lower Homebuilding and Financial Services operating earnings and softer cost leverage on lower revenue.

Company cites persistently elevated mortgage rates, constrained affordability, and cautious consumer sentiment, plus a resurgent inflation reading of 4.2%, as the main headwinds pressuring the quarter.
For Q3 2026, guided 20,500-21,500 deliveries and ~16% gross margin; full-year 2026 delivery target was moderated to approximately 82,000-83,000 homes on interest-rate and geopolitical pressure.
